newsitem.title: USA: May Dept Stores May same store sales rise.
newsitem.headline: May Dept Stores May same store sales rise.

text.p: May Department Stores Co said Thursday that comparable store sales for the four weeks ended May 31, 1997 rose four percent from the same period a year ago.
Preliminary total sales for May increased 9.7 percent to $900.9 million from $821.0 million a year ago.

Comparable store sales for the first four months of fiscal 1997 were up 2.4 percent over last year. Total sales for the first four months of fiscal 1997 were $3.49 billion, up 8.2 percent compared with $3.22 billion during the first four months of fiscal 1996, the retailer said.

Sales have been restated to exclude the sales of stores that have been closed and not replaced. Year-to-date revenues, including sales of nonreplaced closed stores and finance charge revenue, were $3.60 billion in 1997 and $3.36 billion in 1996.

During the month, May said it completed a $300 million stock repurchase program, totaling 6.4 million shares of May stock at an average price of $47 per share. May completed a $600 million stock buyback in January 1997.

Year-to-date, May has opened four new department stores: three Lord & Taylor stores at Willowbrook Mall in Wayne, N.J., Christiana Mall in Newark, Del., and Harrisburg East Mall in Harrisburg, Pa., and one Strawbridge's store at Springfield Mall in Springfield, Pa. An additional nine new department stores are planned for the remainder of the year: three Lord & Taylor stores, one Strawbridge's store, two Foley's stores, and three Filene's stores.
May operates 366 department stores in 30 states and the District of Columbia.
